summary.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 14.9% YoY to INR139.7 crore and EBITDA margin was 40.2%, despite a one-time INR4 crore government receivable write-off.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 14.9% YoY to INR139.7 crore, with EBITDA of INR56.1 crore (40.2% margin) and PAT up 8.6% to INR49.7 crore (31.2% margin). Management said a one-time write-off of a government client's receivable (about INR4 crore gross, INR0.8 crore net P&L hit after a INR3.2 crore offset) cut the EBITDA margin by roughly 4 percentage points, with the balance sitting in other income. The company moved to a new three-segment reporting structure (Automotive, Enterprise, Government) and appointed Rohan Verma as Joint MD. IoT-led revenue rose sharply while Map-led revenue was nearly flat, and management attributed Automotive softness in FY26 H2 to OEM time-shifting rather than contract loss.

segments.name: Automotive
segments.commentary: Revenue INR58.8 crore in Q1 FY27, up 29% YoY from INR45.7 crore; FY26 full year INR190 crore vs INR182 crore in FY25, with H2 FY26 time-shifting of OEM vehicles cited as a drag.

segments.name: Enterprise
segments.commentary: Revenue INR64 crore, up 6% YoY from INR60.6 crore; wins cited across mobility and logistics, BFSI, manufacturing, telecom and renewable energy.

segments.name: Government
segments.commentary: Government revenue was not disclosed for the quarter; management said Q1 is seasonally the weakest quarter for Government and the write-off related to one government client.

segments.name: Map-led vs IoT-led
segments.commentary: Map-led flat at INR98.7 crore (from INR98.2 crore); IoT-led up to INR41 crore from INR23.4 crore, driving consolidated growth.

guidance_outlook: Management reiterated an internal target of 35%+ EBITDA margin for FY27 and declined to guide quarter-by-quarter; asked about 43-44% margins, it said quarterly outcomes will vary.

Open order book at FY26 end was INR1,750 crore, up from INR1,500 crore a year earlier (and about INR1,350 crore before that); management cited it as visibility for future growth but would not comment on quarterly revenue.
Management expects Automotive contract volumes to recover as OEMs change vehicle programmes, but gave no quantitative FY27 Automotive growth target.
International: Southeast Asia JV loss reduced; international revenue not material to P&L in the near term; smaller investments in Middle East and other geographies.
capex_capacity: No capex, capacity or commissioning figures were discussed on the call.
IoT hardware-first growth is expected to convert into SaaS revenue over time, per management.
demand_pricing: Order book split disclosed only annually as fixed-price versus volume-based; not disclosed quarterly for competitive reasons.
Pricing is bespoke, per vehicle, per API transaction, per user or per solution; contract tenure ranges from one to five years with no typical term.
Management said receivables from government are a longer cycle than Automotive and Enterprise; majority of FY26 receivables of INR176 crore were from government (exact share not given).
Digital twin cities opportunity (including Maharashtra's NAKSHA scheme) is being pursued selectively to avoid bad receivables seen at peers.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Automotive OEM contract reduction a 2H FY26 event, and could 2H FY27 be better on a weaker base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was not a contract reduction but time-shifting: one OEM chose not to deploy the technology in some vehicles last year, which may continue, though more vehicles are expected to carry the technology in future.

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA margin run at 43-44% in coming quarters excluding the write-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated a 35%+ full-year margin target and said quarterly margins will vary.

qa_highlights.question: Why is standalone Map-led growth so low and subsidiary revenue down?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said consolidated numbers should be used, as Government and IoT work is routed through subsidiaries; consolidated Map-led was flat at INR98.7 crore while IoT-led rose to INR41 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Order book mix by segment and e-commerce deal progress?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book split by segment was not disclosed; the fixed versus volume split is given annually. Management cited quick commerce and other enterprise wins without quantifying them.

qa_highlights.question: Reconcile the write-off: INR80 lakh P&L impact vs 4% EBITDA margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: The gross INR4 crore receivable was offset by a INR3.2 crore payable not paid; the net INR0.8 crore went to other expense, while the payable saving sat in other income, so the EBITDA margin was hit by about 4 points.

qa_highlights.question: Is IoT services revenue seasonal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said IoT services follow hardware sales with a lag and billing cycles vary (monthly to biennial), so sequential comparisons mislead; Q1 FY27 IoT services INR18 crore vs INR16.3 crore a year earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Is there material international revenue contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: No; management said international revenue is not material and the Southeast Asia JV loss has reduced.

risks_watch: Government receivables: longer collection cycle and a one-time write-off this quarter; watch the government receivable balance and any further write-offs.
Map-led revenue flat YoY at INR98.7 crore; growth is now dependent on IoT-led and Automotive recovery.
IoT hardware-led growth carries lower margin until SaaS converts; margin dilution expected to persist as IoT scales.
Automotive OEM programme timing: continued time-shifting could keep the segment below its potential in the near term.
Southeast Asia JV and other international investments remain loss-making with no near-term material revenue.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the order book and diversification, but evasive on quarterly guidance, segment order mix, pricing and government receivable details, deferring to the investor presentation or offline follow-up.

growth.why: Q1 FY27 revenue grew 14.9% YoY to INR139.7 crore and the open order book rose to INR1,750 crore from INR1,500 crore, but no capacity additions, capex or FY27 revenue guidance were given, and Map-led revenue was flat.
